newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE to go to 4,700 then become unstable.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE to go to 4,700 then become unstable.

text.p: A cautious start to trading on Friday should see the FTSE 100 index crawl up to 4,700, but volatility later in the day will have it bounce around, possibly losing its early gains, technical analysts said.

The past two days have demonstrated the difficulty the market is having in maintaining upward momentum despite rearguard action from pharmaceutical and retail banking stocks which have helped defend the 4,650-4,660 area.
This has technical significance because that level is the one-third retracement target from the FTSE's rise from 4,525 to 4,720. By 0724 GMT, the index was indicated up 8.2 at 4,689.4.

But while the tone has changed slightly from the market's effervescent mood earlier in the week, with every failed attempt to overcome 4,700 on a closing basis and so long as 4,650 holds, there is a reasonable chance the market can advance above 4,700 in the days ahead, analysts said.
Some insecurity after its strong run since mid-April is inevitable but those sectors which have led the market up do not appear to be wobbling out of control yet.
And sellers might be overplaying their hand if they knock the FTSE swiftly down by 100 points because such a move would only take it down to its medium-term supporting trendline.
